Looking forward to interviewing @andrewdfeldman CEO and founder of @cerebras at the @TomorrowXSummit in Austin November 17-18.

Scale-up networking and SRAM acceleration are the best solutions to the DRAM shortage from my perspective. Given that Nebius is monetizing at $20 to $25 per megawatt for long-term contracts, am interested to discuss how Cerebras is going to monetize the 600 megawatts they have under contract for the end of 2027 per their earnings release. Taking a healthy haircut to the Nebius monetization rates given the “take or pay” nature of the OpenAI contract still implies roughly $10b in cloud ARR exiting 2027. Might be upside to this from hardware sales, the AMD partnership, the AWS partnership and the “multiple gigawatt” power pipeline they have. We shall discuss!

LLMs still produce bugs, but those bugs are different than what they used to be. It’s less off-by-ones and more about system design, ui usability, missing broader context. Some kinds of coding has been solved, but not all.

While models continue to improve, adversarial code review has been an incredibly powerful tool to catch many of these kinds of bugs.

It can be as simple as a one line prompt - “use a dynamic workflow to adversarial test every edge case in an iOS simulator”, or use Claude’s built in /code-review (or /code-review low, /code-review medium, etc.)

Towards a future of self-maintaining software.
